anomalies.obs: On sheet 2 the LM1117-5.0 regulator U1 has both its input (pin 1, VI) and its output (pin 2, VO) wired to the +5V net, while the power-input net VCC (from J5 PWR on sheet 1, also feeding R6, JP1 and Q1) is never connected to U1's input.
anomalies.expected: The regulator's input (VI) must sit on the unregulated input rail VCC and its output (VO) on the regulated +5V rail; +5V (which supplies U2/U3, C1/C2, J1 and J3) must be derived from VCC through U1.

evidence.quote: Sheet 2: U1 'LM1117-5.0', pin 1 'VI' -> +5V arrow, pin 2 'VO' -> +5V arrow, pin 3 'GND' -> GND
Sheet 1: J5 'PWR' pin -> VCC; R6 top -> VCC; JP1 pin 2 -> VCC; U2/U3 pin 8 -> +5V

anomalies.impact: The regulator input is shorted to its own 5V output and the actual input rail (VCC) is left disconnected from the regulator, so the +5V rail has no source. The MCU and all +5V loads would be unpowered and the board would not function.

anomalies.obs: R3 is a 10 MΩ resistor between +5V and the RST net (MCU reset, J1 pin 4, J4 RST).
anomalies.expected: A reset pull-up should be on the order of 10 kΩ; 10 MΩ is about 1000× too high and provides essentially no external hold on reset.
anomalies.impact: Reset is only weakly held high externally (relying on the AVR internal pull-up), making the reset line more susceptible to noise and unintended resets.

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: the LM1117-5.0 regulator U1 has its input pin tied to the +5V output rail instead of the VCC input rail, shorting the regulator's I/O and leaving the power input disconnected from the regulator so the MCU's +5V rail is unpowered; a secondary suspicion is the 10 MΩ reset pull-up R3, far higher than the standard ~10 kΩ.
